findings.title: Reject ECDSA integers that exceed the fixed signature width
findings.body: When a decoded DER INTEGER is wider than the expected ECDSA component, this code silently discards its most significant bytes. An oversized value can therefore map to the same fixed-width r or s as a valid signature, so malformed DER signatures are accepted as valid after conversion. Reject out-of-range integers instead of truncating them.

findings.title: Adding an abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public interface, and adding abstract order() breaks compatibility for third-party implementations compiled against the previous interface: provider discovery now invokes order() on them and can fail with AbstractMethodError. Make this a default method with a documented fallback priority, or otherwise preserve compatibility.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider, not Bouncy Castle
findings.body: The provider contract promises a Bouncy Castle security provider, but this returns whichever provider implements the JVM's default keystore type (commonly SUN). Callers that use this method for Bouncy Castle services will receive the wrong provider and may fail or use unintended implementations.

findings.title: The selected global crypto provider leaves most crypto operations unsupported
findings.body: AuthzClient.create initializes the process-wide CryptoIntegration, and this provider can be selected when the authz-client is used without another provider. The selected provider throws UnsupportedOperationException for most CryptoProvider methods, so unrelated Keycloak crypto operations in the same JVM then fail instead of using a complete provider. Implement or delegate the remaining operations, or avoid registering this partial implementation as the global provider.
